author: Autodesk
description: An ocean with waves and spray
documentation:
## Ocean with Foam and Spray

### What it does

This graph generates an ocean surface, including foam and spray from "breaking" waves.

### Inputs and outputs

The inputs for this graph are simulation setting in the `ocean_with_foam` compound.  This compound will generate the ocean surface mesh based on the settings provided including foam and cusp settings.  Influences can be optionally added to the particle simulation that generates spray.  The graph outputs a displaced plane with a *foam* and *foam_colour* attribute and simulated particles for the spray.  The output is renderable.

### How it works

- The *ocean_with_foam* compound creates the ocean surface plane with a spectral displacement appled.  This and a fractal noise is used to generate foam on the ocean surface, and settings for spray generation are included in the output. Please dive into this compound to see how this is achieved.

- After the velocity is scaled to avoid extreme values, the `simulate_spray_particles` compound emits particles from the ocean surface, based on surface properties.  It's here that you can optionally connect any particle influences to affect the spray - adding a wind for example.  Again, inside this compound are notes and instructions.

- The final displaced result is then shaded and output.

metadata.description: An ocean with waves and spray

_notes.text: This is a basic spectral ocean simulation with foam and particle spray.
Simulate the spectral waves with foam and create and displace a plane mesh with the waves.

Scale the wave velocity and avoid extreme values. This velocity is used by the particle inherit_velocity. The xz velocity is exaggerated a bit to make particles emit more horizontally for crashing wave effects.

Emit and simulate particles. The foam cusp values and wave speed are used for the particle emission. They were set as vertex properties "cusp" and "point_velocity" on the mesh inside the ocean_with_foam compound.
The particle *sources*, *influences* and *colliders* have been exposed so that they can be connected to, try connecting this ***wind_influence***
Determine the resolution from the bounds and detail_size and create a plane mesh to displace.

Construct a fractal noise field to map the cusp scale with so the foam has more detail. This especially helps when *add_mode* is enabled. The noise is animated and thresholded creating a swirly foam pattern.

***wave_set_foam*** has been made editable so that "cusp" from the foam simulation can be set per vertex, in addition to the "foam" property. 
This will be used in the particle emission.
***displace_by_wave*** has been made editable to additionally set the "point_velocity" property from the wave speed, in addition to displacing the mesh.
The velocity is set here so it can be used in particle emission.
The cusp is set here so it can be used in particle emission.
This sets up the particle emission using the *cusp* and *point_velocity* properties from the wave and foam simulation.
This uses the gradient of a fractal noise to push particles into a stringy shape over time. Too much drag will make the emission like smoke.
This compound deletes particles that are below the mesh by raytracing upward from particle positions. (post simulation)
This influence kills particles during simulation when they go below a height value.
We create a custom property -  *drag_scale* (used  in ***noise_gradient_drag_influence***) so that some particles can be more affected by drag.
The dot here is negative when the emission velocity would go inside the water, so we avoid emitting in that case
